games.recap: Played by Joe in the playable app and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat on 2026-11-09 as four files: the full graded play by play, the scorecard CSV export, the app scorecard PDF (the Payoff Pitch Gazette, Final Edition, Monday, November 9, 2026), and the scorecard photo. Joe ruled in chat the same day: "Use this replace Tigers game 6," adopting this playing as the new R1-04 Game 6 under the R1-05, R1-06, and R1-10 Game 1 adoption precedents and the R1-01 Game 1, Game 2, Game 3, and Game 4 adoptions of 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09; the replaced game (Detroit 10, Arizona 3; W Hal Newhouser, L Randy Johnson, SV Willie Hernandez; seed 20261213), the old series clincher, is preserved untouched in the Diamondbacks records at archive/replaced/. The series result is unchanged, Detroit winning the series 4-2, the adopted game being the clincher as the replaced game was; series runs move from 25 to 14 to 28 to 15, and both club records are unchanged, Detroit having won the replaced game as well. The replacement was made as a guarded manual edit under Joe's ruling, confined to this game object, its detail file, and the series entry's MVP line, runner-up line, and Game 6 narrative. The Series MVP stays Harry Heilmann, on Joe's standing ruling; Heilmann does not appear in the adopted game, so his MVP line is recomputed from Games 1 to 5 as now booked and reads "1 for 11, 1 2B, 0 RBI, 2 R, .091", where it read "4 for 16, 2 2B, 1 HR, 7 RBI, 3 R, .250" with the replaced game inside it. Joe's 2026-11-08 ruling that settled the replaced game's Top 7 RBI ambiguity for Heilmann, and the offset question it left open (the replaced game's Detroit lines totaling 11 RBI for 10 runs, and its game recap still reading 6 RBI), belong to the replaced game's preserved history now and are superseded for the book by this adoption. The runner-up line is recomputed the same way: George Kell, "7 for 21, 3 3B, 3 RBI, 1 R, .333" (the stored line had also gone stale on the 2026-11-08 corrections, which had already moved his Game 3 RBI to 1). All four sources agree on every number: the linescore, the batting and pitching sums, plate appearances against batters faced for every pitcher (Detroit 46 against Johnson's 15, Kim's 5, Chafin's 6, Valverde's 3, Bradley's 5, Ziegler's 5, Putz's 4, and Schilling's 3; Arizona 34 against Newhouser's 34), and printed RBI (Detroit 12 for 13, the one run without a printed RBI being Cabrera's in the Top 7, which scored on Moreno's second passed ball of Freehan's plate appearance; Arizona 4 for 4), booked exactly as printed. No seed is printed in any source, so rng_seed is 0, as in the R1-06, R1-10, and R1-01 adoptions. The decisions are printed in the log: Hal Newhouser takes the win with a complete game (9.0 IP, 3 H, 4 R, 4 ER, 6 BB, 1 HB, 6 SO, 1 HR) and Randy Johnson the loss (2.2 IP, 6 H, 6 R, 6 ER, 1 BB, 2 SO, 2 HR); there is no save, Arizona using eight pitchers. Detroit scored three in the 2nd on Freehan's three-run home run off Johnson (Greenberg and Veach aboard), three in the 3rd on Veach's three-run home run off Johnson (Gehringer and Cabrera aboard), two in the 5th off Chafin (Kaline on Veach's forceout, Greenberg on Freehan's sacrifice fly), three in the 7th (Kaline's solo home run off Bradley; Cabrera on Moreno's second passed ball of Freehan's plate appearance against Bradley; and Veach on Freehan's single off Bradley, both runs after the homer unearned as printed because the passed balls moved both runners), and two in the 9th on Freehan's two-run home run off Putz (Cabrera aboard). Arizona scored two in the 5th on Williams's two-run home run off Newhouser (Finley aboard) and two in the 7th (Gonzalez on Williams's single, Walker thrown out at the plate on Kaline's throw on the same play, and Finley on Moreno's forceout). Freehan finished 4 for 4 with two home runs and 7 RBI; Veach drove in 4. The game was errorless. Hit batters: Finley, hit by Newhouser in the Bottom 9 (the log adds that the batter charged the mound; no ejection or injury is recorded in any source and none is booked). Wild pitches: Newhouser 1 and Putz 1, as printed; passed balls: Moreno 2, as printed. Sacrifice flies: Freehan (Top 5), the game's only one; sacrifice hits: none. Grounded into double plays: Walker (Bottom 2), Trammell (Top 7), and Goldschmidt (Bottom 8). Stolen bases: none, and no runner was caught stealing. Substitutes: none on either club; Detroit used nine men, Arizona nine men and eight pitchers. Defensive lines are booked as a defense object in the established shape, under the same replay exception Joe directed for the R1-01 replays (a Round 1 game carrying defense because the replay was played with full tracking); Detroit's 27 putouts and 13 assists and Arizona's 27 putouts and 12 assists are exactly the printed fielding tables. Graded decisions, narrated here because final_grades stays empty as in every app-era game in this archive: Bob Brenly (Arizona) 8 (2 paid off, 3 backfired, 3 neutral): the Top 3 change to Kim neutral (-0.15), the Top 5 change to Chafin backfired (-1.77), the Top 5 leave-in of a fatigued Chafin paid off (+0.47), the Top 6 change to Valverde paid off (+0.73), the Top 7 change to Bradley backfired (-2.77), the Top 7 change to Ziegler neutral (+0.26), the Top 9 change to Putz backfired (-1.27), and the Top 9 change to Schilling neutral (-0.15). Sparky Anderson (Detroit) 1: the Bottom 9 leave-in of a fatigued Newhouser paid off (+0.73). Managers: Sparky Anderson (Detroit) and Bob Brenly (Arizona). Venue is Chase Field. Detroit won the series 4-2.

Played by Joe in the playable app and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat on 2026-11-09 as four files: the full graded play by play, the scorecard CSV export, the app scorecard PDF (the Payoff Pitch Gazette, Final Edition, Monday, November 9, 2026), and the scorecard photo. Joe's instruction in chat the same day: "Game 2 cubs replacement," adopting this playing as the new R1-06 Game 2 under the R1-05, R1-06, and R1-10 Game 1 adoption precedents, the R1-01 Game 1 through Game 4 adoptions of 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09, and the R1-04 Game 6 adoption earlier on 2026-11-09; the replaced game (Montreal 4, Chicago 2; W Pedro Martinez, L Pedro Strop, SV John Wetteland, all derived; played 2026-10-29) is preserved untouched in the Cubs records at archive/replaced/, with a README closing the reconstruction episode described below. The series result is unchanged, Chicago winning the series 4-1, Montreal having won Game 2 in both playings; series runs move from 24 to 14 to 25 to 15, and both club records are unchanged. The replacement was made as a guarded manual edit under Joe's ruling, confined to this game object, its detail file, and the series entry's MVP line. The Series MVP stays Ron Santo, on Joe's 2026-11-08 ruling ("Keep Santo as R1-06 MVP"); Santo went 0 for 5 in the adopted game, so his MVP line is recomputed from the five games as now booked and reads "4 for 22, 2 R, 2 2B, 1 HR, 3 RBI, .182", where it read "6 for 21, 4 R, 3 2B, 2 HR, 4 RBI, .286" with the replaced game inside it. The replaced game was one of the tournament's two lines-only games: its scorecard log under-records one base state (Top 7, whether Ron Fairly tagged at second on Orlando Cabrera's fly out to center), its play-by-play never converted, and it carried no defense object. A box-score reconstruction PDF offered on 2026-11-08 as a cure was rejected because it rewrote two recorded plays (a Raines double became a single, and Cabrera's fly out became a groundout advancing Fairly); Joe chose the replay cure instead, and this adopted game, played with full tracking, carries its defense object under the same replay exception as the R1-01 replays and the R1-04 Game 6 adoption. All four sources agree on every number: the linescore, the batting and pitching sums, plate appearances against batters faced for every pitcher (Montreal 45 against Brown's 26, Sutter's 6, Lee Smith's 4, Strop's 3, Marshall's 3, and Wood's 3; Chicago 43 against Pedro Martinez's 25, Reardon's 5, Rojas's 4, Wetteland's 3, Burke's 3, and McGaffigan's 3), and printed RBI (Montreal 5 for 5, Chicago 3 for 3), booked exactly as printed. No seed is printed in any source, so rng_seed is 0, as in the other adoptions. The decisions are not printed in any source and are derived by the run charges: Tim Burke takes the win (a scoreless Bottom 10, and he was the pitcher of record when Montreal took the lead in the Top 11), Sean Marshall the loss (both Top 11 runs his: Gary Carter's single and Andre Dawson's two-run home run), and Andy McGaffigan the save (he entered the Bottom 11 up two, threw a scoreless inning, and finished the game). Chicago scored first, in the Bottom 3: Pete Crow-Armstrong walked, stole second on the play Jose Vidro dropped Gary Carter's throw (the game's only error, E4), moved to third on Ryne Sandberg's groundout, and scored on Anthony Rizzo's single. Billy Williams's solo home run off Pedro Martinez made it 2-0 in the Bottom 4. Montreal took the lead in the Top 6 off Mordecai Brown: Vidro singled, Larry Walker hit a two-run home run, Vladimir Guerrero grounded out, and Gary Carter homered. Chicago tied it in the Bottom 7 off Jeff Reardon: Gabby Hartnett singled, Crow-Armstrong bunted him to second, and Rizzo singled him home. The game stayed 3-3 until the Top 11, when Carter singled off Marshall and Dawson followed with a two-run home run. Brown started for Chicago (6.1 IP, 7 H, 3 R, 3 ER, 0 BB, 1 HB, 5 SO, 2 HR) and Pedro Martinez for Montreal (6.0 IP, 6 H, 2 R, 2 ER, 2 BB, 8 SO, 1 HR); twelve pitchers appeared in all. The only error is Vidro's; Chicago turned the game's only double play (Tim Wallach's Top 5 grounder, Banks to Sandberg to Rizzo); Ernie Banks was caught stealing in the Bottom 4 on the hit-and-run strikeout (Carter's throw, Cabrera covering), and Crow-Armstrong's Bottom 3 steal is the game's only stolen base. Wild pitch: Brown 1, as printed; passed balls: none. Crow-Armstrong's Bottom 7 bunt is the game's only sacrifice, and there are no sacrifice flies. Brian Schneider replaced Carter at catcher for the Bottom 11 (a graded defensive sub, below); he had no plate appearance and no fielding chance (the inning's outs were Dawson's fly to center, Cabrera's 6-3 groundout, and Raines's fly to left), so no batting or defense line is carried for him, his appearance standing in the graded log and in this record. Defensive lines are booked as a defense object in the established shape, under the replay exception above: Montreal's 33 putouts and 14 assists and Chicago's 33 putouts and 9 assists are exactly the printed fielding tables. Graded decisions, narrated here because final_grades stays empty as in every app-era game in this archive: Frank Chance (Chicago) 10 (5 paid off, 3 backfired, 2 neutral), the best his Top 7 change to Bruce Sutter with Wallach on third (+1.20) and the worst his Top 11 change to Sean Marshall (-1.27); Dick Williams (Montreal) 7 (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 2 neutral), his one backfire the Bottom 7 change to Jeff Reardon (-0.77), and his Bottom 11 change to McGaffigan and the Schneider defensive sub both paying off. Game 3 availability: under this adopted game Pedro Martinez threw 18 outs and Brown 19 (the replaced game had 24 and 18), both still in the unavailable band for Game 3, and every other arm threw five outs or fewer and stays free, so Game 3's availability was honored identically under either playing; a dated provenance note is appended to Game 3's official record, and its data stands as played. Managers: Frank Chance (Chicago) and Dick Williams (Montreal). Venue is Wrigley Field. Chicago won the series 4-1.

Played by Joe in the fixed app build and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat on 2026-11-09 as six files: the box score CSV export carrying the new PLAYS (JSON) section, a second CSV whose printed sections are identical to the first (the same export sent twice), the standalone plays JSON holding the same rows as the CSV's PLAYS section, the app scorecard PDF (the Payoff Pitch Gazette), the full graded play-by-play text, and the app's full Rec JSON record; official L1-02 Game 4 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Losers Bracket Round 1, Series 2: the Baltimore Orioles (seed 15) against the Washington Nationals (seed 31), from the reseeded pool of the 16 opening-round losers, paired highest against lowest in pairing order. Both clubs carry one series loss into this series, so the loser of this series is eliminated and the winner survives to Losers Round 2. Home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 4 at Nationals Park in Washington, with Game 5 back at Baltimore next. Box score record: the sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, the fielding lines, a complete graded play log, and the game's full play rows, and they agree on every printed number, with the decisions settled here and documented, the sources governing throughout. The decisions are not printed in the Gazette, the CSV, or the log and are derived from the play log and the run charges on the card; the app's stored record (the Rec JSON) carries the identical three names in its own W, L, and S fields, corroborating the derivation exactly. Tippy Martinez takes the win: he threw a scoreless Bottom 10 (Harper struck out, Rendon grounded out to second, Zimmerman grounded out to short) and was Baltimore's pitcher of record when his club took the lead for good in the Top 11. Sean Burnett takes the loss: he pitched both extra innings for Washington, a scoreless Top 10, and the Top 11 run (Blair's triple and Anderson's sacrifice fly) is charged to his line as printed. Stu Miller takes the save: he threw a scoreless Bottom 11 (Murphy flied out to left, Johnson grounded out to short, Ramos flied out to right) protecting a one-run lead and finished the game, the save on the lead-of-three-or-fewer plus at-least-one-inning prong. The starters took no decisions: Mike Cuellar (8.0 IP, 7 H, 3 R, 3 ER, 4 BB, 2 SO, 1 HR) left after the Bottom 8 with the game tied 3-3 on Zimmerman's home run, and Gio Gonzalez (6.0 IP, 8 H, 3 R, 3 ER, 3 BB, 3 SO, 1 HR) left after the Top 6 with Washington trailing 3-0 and never held a lead. Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Washington pitching allows 4 (Gonzalez 3, Rauch 0, Storen 0, Cordero 0, Burnett 1), and Baltimore pitching allows 3 (Cuellar 3, Olson 0, Tippy Martinez 0, Miller 0). Every run in the game is earned as printed; there is no earned-run settlement in this game. The duplicate test ran before the number was assigned: the series had three stored games, Baltimore 6, Washington 1 in Game 1, Washington 6, Baltimore 4 in Game 2, and Baltimore 9, Washington 5 in Game 3, all different linescores, so this box score takes Game 4. The game: Baltimore struck in the Top 1, Anderson and Frank Robinson singling to the corners and Murray's sacrifice fly scoring Anderson. Washington's Bottom 1 hit and run moved Turner to second on Soto's groundout but Harper grounded out behind it. Baltimore added two in the Top 3: Blair hit a solo home run off Gonzalez, Grich doubled, Anderson bunted him to third, and after Frank Robinson struck out, Murray doubled Grich home for 3-0. Washington did nothing with Rendon's Bottom 2 walk and Johnson's two-out single, and the middle innings went quiet: Dempsey's Top 4 bunt forced Brooks Robinson at second, and Baltimore left the bases loaded in the Top 6 when Anderson flied out to left against a fatigued Gonzalez left in by the book. Washington's comeback came one run at a time. In the Bottom 6 Turner singled, did not get a good jump on the steal call and stayed put, Soto doubled him to third, and after Harper struck out and Rendon walked to load the bases, Zimmerman's forceout at second scored Turner, the run earned as printed, for 3-1. In the Bottom 7, with Sisler just in at first base for Murray, Ramos and Span singled, Turner's forceout put runners at the corners, and Soto singled Ramos home for 3-2. In the Bottom 8 Zimmerman hit a solo home run off Cuellar to tie it 3-3, Weaver leaving his fatigued starter in and the next two batters going quietly. The ninth and tenth stayed scoreless: Frank Robinson doubled off Cordero in the Top 9 but Sisler lined out and Powell flied out; Olson struck out Span and Soto around Turner's double in the Bottom 9; Burnett's Top 10 ended on Harper's range play on Ripken's deep fly to right; and Tippy Martinez threw a perfect Bottom 10. The Top 11 decided it: Blair tripled off Burnett, Grich grounded out with the infield in and Blair held, and Anderson's sacrifice fly to center scored him for 4-3. Miller closed the Bottom 11 in order. Baltimore stranded 11 and Washington 9. Home runs: two, Blair's solo shot in the Top 3 off Gonzalez and Zimmerman's solo shot in the Bottom 8 off Cuellar. Doubles: six, Grich, Murray, Powell, and Frank Robinson for Baltimore and Soto and Turner for Washington. Triples: one, Blair's in the Top 11, the game's decisive hit. Errors: none, an errorless game both ways, and errors_by is empty in the established shape. Hit batters: none; HB 0 for every pitcher and HBP 0 for every batter are carried as card-sourced values, so the hit batter check runs on real data. Wild pitches: none, the CSV printing WP 0 for all nine pitchers. Passed balls: none, the fielding tables printing PB 0 for Dempsey and for Ramos. Sacrifices: three: Anderson's sacrifice bunt in the Top 3 and the two sacrifice flies, Murray's in the Top 1 and Anderson's in the Top 11; Dempsey's Top 4 bunt is a fielder's choice at-bat (the lead runner forced, the batter safe), not a sacrifice, and reads SH 0. Stolen bases: none, and none caught; Martinez sent Turner in the Bottom 6 and Turner did not get a good jump and stayed put, the sources charging no attempt, and each catcher reads no steals against. Double plays grounded into: none; no double play was turned, the three forceout plays (Murray Top 5, Zimmerman Bottom 6, Turner Bottom 7) being fielder's choices, not double plays. Substitutions: one: George Sisler replacing Eddie Murray at first base as a defensive sub for the Bottom 7 for Baltimore, then batting once (a lineout to third in the Top 9), so he carries both a batting line (AB 1) and a defense players line (6 putouts, including both Bottom 10 putouts on the Rendon and Zimmerman groundouts and the Bottom 11 Johnson groundout); Washington made none and prints nine batting lines, Baltimore ten. Defensive lines are built with this booking under Joe's 2026-11-07 standing instruction: errors_by is empty because the game was errorless, and a defense object in the established shape (Baltimore 33 putouts and 17 assists, Washington 33 putouts and 9 assists; Dempsey's 5 catcher putouts are exactly Washington's 5 strikeouts, and Ramos's 7 are exactly Baltimore's 7 strikeouts, with no caught stealing to adjust either tie; Harper's Top 10 range out on Ripken's deep fly is carried in his fielding row's range column and in the play rows, the defense object carrying putouts, assists, and errors in the established shape; wild pitches true zeros for all nine pitchers as the CSV prints, and passed balls true zeros for both catchers). Plate appearances counted fresh from the printed batting lines and the play log, a runner out on the bases counting as one of the inning's outs and never an add-on: Baltimore PA is AB 41 plus BB 4 plus SH 1 plus SF 2, which is 48, and the outs plus runs plus stranded identity agrees (33 outs plus 4 runs plus 11 stranded is 48); Washington PA is AB 41 plus BB 4, which is 45, and the identity agrees (33 outs plus 3 runs plus 9 stranded is 45). Batters faced tie to those totals: Baltimore 48 PA against 48 Washington BF (Gonzalez 29, Rauch 5, Storen 3, Cordero 4, Burnett 7), and Washington 45 PA against 45 Baltimore BF (Cuellar 35, Olson 4, Tippy Martinez 3, Miller 3), counted from the card. Strikeouts tie both ways: Baltimore batting 7 against Washington pitching 7 (Gonzalez 3, Storen 2, Cordero 1, Burnett 1), and Washington batting 5 against Baltimore pitching 5 (Cuellar 2, Olson 2, Tippy Martinez 1). Printed RBI: Baltimore 4 for 4 (Murray 2, Anderson 1, Blair 1) and Washington 3 for 3 (Zimmerman 2, Soto 1); every run in the game carried an RBI. The game's play rows travel with the sources for the first time under the new export: the 103 rows in the CSV's PLAYS (JSON) section and the standalone plays JSON were gated against the printed lines before booking (every batting and pitching line rebuilt from the rows alone exactly, batters faced included, the linescore rebuilt exactly, the rows' run totals 4 and 3, and the win probability chain closing at zero), and they are staged with the booking for the tournament's play-by-play store. Availability from Game 3 was honored: McNally (21 outs in Game 3) and Zimmermann (18 outs) were unavailable and neither pitched, Zimmermann not appearing in the game at all, every other arm on both clubs was free, and all usage stayed inside it. Availability for Game 5, read from Game 4 outs under the standing convention (under 6 outs free, 6 to 8 outs capped at 3, 9 or more unavailable): Cuellar (24 outs) and Gonzalez (18 outs) are unavailable, Burnett (6 outs) is capped at 3 outs, and every other arm used in Game 4 (Olson, Tippy Martinez, and Miller at 3 outs each, Rauch, Storen, and Cordero at 3 outs each) is free. Twelve decisions were graded. Dave Martinez (Washington) made 7 (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 2 neutral): the Bottom 1 hit and run backfired at -0.76 (Soto grounded out and no runs scored in the rest of the inning), the game's worst grade; the Top 6 leave-in of Gonzalez, fatigued by the book, paid off at +0.73 (Ripken popped out and the bases-loaded threat died with no runs); the Bottom 6 steal was neutral at +0.14 (Turner held, one run scoring in the rest of the inning); the Top 7 pitching change to Rauch was neutral at +0.23 (Frank Robinson walked, no runs); the Top 8 pitching change to Storen paid off at +0.73; the Top 9 pitching change to Cordero paid off at +0.73; and the Top 10 pitching change to Burnett paid off at +0.73. Earl Weaver (Baltimore) made 5 (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 0 neutral): the Bottom 7 defensive sub of Sisler at first base backfired at -0.52 (a clean inning in the field, one run scoring in the rest of the inning); the Bottom 8 leave-in of Cuellar, fatigued by the book, paid off at +0.50 (Murphy grounded out after the tying home run, no more runs); the Bottom 9 pitching change to Olson paid off at +0.73; the Bottom 10 pitching change to Tippy Martinez paid off at +0.73; and the Bottom 11 pitching change to Miller paid off at +0.73. Managers: Earl Weaver (Baltimore) and Dave Martinez (Washington). Venue is Nationals Park. Baltimore leads the series 3-1, and Washington faces elimination in Game 5 at Baltimore.

Played by Joe in the app and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat on 2026-11-09 as four files: the box score CSV export carrying the PLAYS (JSON) section, the standalone plays JSON holding the same rows as the CSV's PLAYS section, the app scorecard PDF (the Payoff Pitch Gazette), and the full graded play-by-play text; official L1-02 Game 5 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Losers Bracket Round 1, Series 2: the Baltimore Orioles (seed 15) against the Washington Nationals (seed 31), from the reseeded pool of the 16 opening-round losers, paired highest against lowest in pairing order. Baltimore leads the series 3-1, so Washington plays to survive and Baltimore to close it out. Home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 5 at Oriole Park at Camden Yards in Baltimore. Box score record: the sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, the fielding lines, a complete graded play log, and the game's full play rows, and they agree on every printed number, with the decisions settled here and documented, the sources governing throughout. Mike Flanagan takes the win: he threw a complete game (9.0 IP, 8 H, 4 R, 4 ER, 7 BB, 8 SO, 0 HR, 41 batters faced) and was never relieved, his club taking the lead for good while he was the pitcher of record in the Bottom 7. Sean Burnett takes the loss: he pitched the Bottom 7, walked Murray, and Murray scored the go-ahead run on Ripken's double, the run charged to Burnett's line as printed (1.0 IP, 1 H, 1 R, 1 ER, 1 BB, 1 SO, 5 batters faced). There is no save: Flanagan finished the game himself. Livan Hernandez took no decision (6.0 IP, 8 H, 4 R, 4 ER, 2 BB, 3 SO, 29 batters faced): he left after the Bottom 6 with the game tied 4-4. Stephen Strasburg threw a scoreless Bottom 8 (1.0 IP, 3 batters faced, 1 strikeout). Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Washington pitching allows 5 (Hernandez 4, Burnett 1, Strasburg 0), and Baltimore pitching allows 4 (Flanagan 4). The duplicate test ran before the number was assigned: the series had four stored games, Baltimore 6, Washington 1 in Game 1, Washington 6, Baltimore 4 in Game 2, Baltimore 9, Washington 5 in Game 3, and Baltimore 4, Washington 3 in 11 innings in Game 4, all different linescores, so this box score takes Game 5. The game: nobody scored through five innings. Flanagan worked around traffic all night: Turner's Top 1 single, Rendon's Top 2 walk, back-to-back walks to Turner and Soto in the Top 3, and Nick Johnson's two-out double in the Top 4 putting runners at second and third before Ramos popped out to short. Baltimore's best early chances died the same quiet way: Ripken doubled in the Bottom 2 and Brooks Robinson singled him to third, but Dempsey struck out and Blair grounded out to third; in the Bottom 4 Brooks Robinson doubled and Dempsey bunted him to third, but Blair grounded out to short; and Turner's error on Anderson's Bottom 3 grounder put two aboard with one out and Baltimore came away empty. Washington broke through in the Top 6: Harper walked, Rendon and Zimmerman singled to load the bases with nobody out, Murphy doubled two runs home to right, Johnson's groundout to short scored Zimmerman, and Ramos doubled Murphy home for 4-0; Span flied out and Turner struck out behind it. Baltimore answered in the same half inning: Murray and Powell singled, Ripken doubled both of them home, Brooks Robinson walked, Dempsey bunted the runners to second and third, and Blair singled two runs home to tie the game 4-4; Martinez left the fatigued Hernandez in and it paid off on the card, Grich lining out to short and Anderson flying out to left to end the inning. The Bottom 7 decided the series: Burnett, pitching the one inning his Game 4 workload allowed him, struck out Frank Robinson, walked Murray, and got Powell's flyout to center, and Ripken doubled Murray home for 5-4, the third of Ripken's three doubles on the night. Sisler took over at first base for the Top 8, and the double play he finished, Brooks Robinson starting it on Johnson's grounder after Zimmerman and Murphy had opened the inning with singles, killed Washington's last real threat; Ramos struck out behind it. Strasburg threw a perfect Bottom 8. In the Top 9 Flanagan, left in by the book while fatigued, retired Span and Turner, walked Soto and Harper with two out, and ended the game and the series on Rendon's popout to Grich. Washington stranded 10 and Baltimore 8. Home runs: none, a series clincher with no ball leaving the park; the game's only extra-base hits are seven doubles, three of them Ripken's plus Brooks Robinson's for Baltimore and Murphy's, Johnson's, and Ramos's for Washington. Plate appearances counted fresh from the printed batting lines and the play log, a runner out on the bases counting as one of the inning's outs and never an add-on: Washington PA is AB 34 plus BB 7, which is 41, and the outs plus runs plus stranded identity agrees (27 outs plus 4 runs plus 10 stranded is 41); Baltimore PA is AB 32 plus BB 3 plus SH 2, which is 37, and the identity agrees (24 outs plus 5 runs plus 8 stranded is 37). Availability from Game 4 was honored: Cuellar (24 outs in Game 4) and Gonzalez (18 outs) were unavailable and neither pitched; Burnett (6 outs in Game 4) was capped at 3 outs for this game and recorded exactly 3, the cap met to the out in the inning that beat him; Flanagan and Hernandez did not pitch in Game 4 and were free, and Strasburg (3 outs in Game 4) was free. Eight decisions were graded. Dave Martinez (Washington) made 6 (2 paid off, 3 backfired, 1 neutral): all three of his steal sends backfired with the runner held each time, the Top 1 and Top 4 sends at -0.51 each and the Top 8 send of Zimmerman the game's worst grade at -0.86 (no runs scored in the rest of the inning against 0.86 expected); the Bottom 6 leave-in of Hernandez, fatigued by the book, paid off at +0.76 (Grich lined out, no runs scored in the rest of the inning); the Bottom 7 pitching change to Burnett was neutral at -0.27 (the go-ahead run scored in the rest of the inning against 0.48 expected); and the Bottom 8 pitching change to Strasburg paid off at +0.73. Earl Weaver (Baltimore) made 2 (2 paid off, 0 backfired, 0 neutral): the Top 8 defensive sub of Sisler at first base paid off at +0.48 (a clean inning in the field that turned the game's only double play), and the Top 9 leave-in of Flanagan, fatigued by the book, paid off at +0.73 (Span flied out, no runs scored in the rest of the inning). Managers: Earl Weaver (Baltimore) and Dave Martinez (Washington). Venue is Oriole Park at Camden Yards. Baltimore wins the series 4-1: Washington is eliminated, the second club out of the tournament after Philadelphia, and Baltimore advances to Losers Round 2.
